Hi Priya — thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps to unblock procurement: 

- Commercial paths we covered: (A) Pilot via corporate card / marketplace for small pilots (fastest), or (B) PO + vendor onboarding for formal contracts and Net terms.
- You mentioned AP prefers PO for anything over ~$10k and often uses Net30. Please confirm thresholds.
- Items we'll need to move forward on the PO path: vendor packet (W-9 / tax form), vendor risk questionnaire, and a short SOW.

I attached a one-pager pricing summary to help Quantiva build an internal PO. If the marketplace route is easier for your pilot, we can enable a card-based pilot and follow up with vendor onboarding in parallel.

Proposed next steps:
1) Priya — confirm which path you prefer (card pilot vs PO) and any internal thresholds/timing.
2) If PO: send vendor onboarding checklist (see attached) + our draft SOW, and we’ll return the filled packet within 24-48 business hours.
3) If card: tell us the billing contact and card limits; we can provision a trial environment and provide an invoice for card reconciliation.

Attachments: redwood-pricing-summary.pdf

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick 15-min call if useful.

Hi Logan — thanks for the clear notes and the summary. A few clarifications from procurement: 

- Thresholds: AP requires a PO for any vendor spend > $10,000 annually. For pilots under $5,000 we typically allow corporate card. Between $5k-10k is reviewed case-by-case.
- Terms: standard is Net30 but the PO needs a vendor code and a completed vendor packet (W-9 + vendor risk form) before a PO is issued.
- Marketplace: we do use Azure Marketplace for a subset of SaaS vendors; being listed there speeds the pilot-to-production path (finance prefers marketplace billing if available).

Can you confirm: do you have a marketplace listing or a billing-as-a-service option? Also please send the vendor packet and a sample PO (or DocuSign link) so I can circulate internally.

Timeline: if we receive the vendor packet this week, procurement could issue a PO within ~7 business days (pending vendor checks).

Thanks —
Priya Shah
Director, Procurement | Quantiva Labs

Thanks Priya — appreciated. Quick answers and attachments in-line: 

- Marketplace: Redwood is available via the Azure Marketplace (we can provide the listing ID). Marketplace billing is supported and would let you pilot on card and transition cleanly.

- Vendor packet: attaching our vendor_onboarding_checklist.xlsx and a draft SOW (redwood-sow-draft.docx). The packet includes our W-9 stub and vendor risk contact. If you prefer, we can send formal W-9 as a signed PDF.

- PO path timing: we’ll return completed paperwork within 48 hours once you confirm the required fields for the vendor packet and the bill-to address. We can also accept Net30 on the PO path.

Two suggested commercial routes depending on your timeline:
A) Fast pilot: marketplace / card — enable pilot within 2 business days; billing via card and standard marketplace reconciliation.
B) Formal PO: we’ll complete vendor forms and SOW; procurement issues PO and we accept Net30. Expect ~7 business days for PO issuance after forms submitted.

Attachments: vendor_onboarding_checklist.xlsx; redwood-sow-draft.docx

If useful I can open a short DocuSign PO for signature. Which would you prefer?

Best,
Logan
